speaker: Doctor
text: I'll start by asking about the onset of your symptoms. When did you first notice the double vision, and has it been constant or intermittent?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest is highly suggestive of myasthenia gravis. Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or speaking, or perhaps droopy eyelids? Also, do you take any medications regularly?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR antibodies; REQUEST TEST: Repetitive Nerve Stimulation (RNS). Have you experienced any recent respiratory infections, and do you have any history of thymoma?
